events.title: Iran launched retaliatory missile and drone strikes across the Gulf region
events.summary: In response to the U.S. and Israeli strikes, Iran launched missiles and drones at Israel and across the Gulf region on February 28. Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE, and Bahrain reported strikes or interceptions. Saudi Arabia said it had been targeted in Riyadh and its Eastern Province and claimed to have intercepted the attacks. Residential areas in Dubai were hit. Jordan intercepted Iranian missiles over its territory. Syria reported civilian fatalities from an Iranian missile strike, with at least four civilians killed. One woman was killed in a strike on Tel Aviv, according to Israel's Magen David Adom emergency service, with additional injuries reported across Israel. Iran threatened to shut the Strait of Hormuz and warned vessels, a corridor through which roughly one-fifth of global oil consumption passes, immediately spiking global disruption fears.
events.why_relevant: Retaliatory strikes by Iran pulled multiple regional nations into active hostilities without their choice, escalated civilian casualties across multiple countries, and threatened critical global energy infrastructure, destabilizing the region and global economy.
events.federal_nexus: U.S. military operations triggered the Iranian retaliation; U.S. interests and allies were directly targeted.

events.title: Shajareh Tayyebeh girls' elementary school struck in Minab, Iran
events.summary: A missile struck the Shajareh Tayyebeh girls' elementary school in Minab, Iran's Hormozgan province, during class change. Victims were between seven and twelve years old. The Washington Post, New York Times, Reuters, and Iranian fact-checking organization Factnameh verified footage of the destroyed school as authentic. The school was located near an IRGC naval base that was targeted in a separate strike. Iranian sources report death toll between 108 and 165, with approximately 95 injured, the overwhelming majority schoolgirls. The Washington Post reported no independent confirmation of casualty numbers. The Israeli military said it was unaware of strikes in the area; the U.S. military said it was "looking into" the reports. UNESCO condemned the attack as a grave violation of international humanitarian law.
events.why_relevant: The strike on a civilian school contradicts the administration's public characterization of the operation as "precision" and "pinpoint," raising questions about targeting accuracy and civilian protection in an undeclared war.
events.federal_nexus: U.S. military operations conducted the strikes; the school destruction occurred as part of Operation Epic Fury.

events.title: Strike on Minab girls' elementary school in Iran killed dozens of children
events.summary: A girls' elementary school in Minab, a city in Iran's southern Hormozgan province, was struck during the February 28 military campaign. Death toll figures varied widely and remained unverified under blackout conditions. Early Iranian reporting cited 108 killed; ABC News reported Iranian leaders and state TV said 115 were dead as of Saturday evening ET. Tasnim and Fars, Iranian state-aligned news agencies, reported the victims were elementary-aged children, with Middle East Eye citing ages between 7 and 12. A CENTCOM spokesperson told ABC News the U.S. was "looking into" reports of the school strike and emphasized that the U.S. does not target civilians. The strike itself was widely reported by AP, NPR, Al Jazeera, ABC News, Middle East Eye, and the Washington Post, though casualty figures remained provisional and unverified due to the communications blackout.
events.why_relevant: A confirmed strike on a civilian school housing elementary-aged children resulted in mass casualties, raising questions about targeting procedures, civilian protection, and accountability in military operations.
events.federal_nexus: U.S. military forces participated in the strike campaign; CENTCOM acknowledged investigating the school strike.

events.summary: President Trump announced "major combat operations in Iran" on Saturday, March 1, 2026, despite U.S. intelligence assessments that Iran posed no imminent threat. The military action followed private calls in which Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman urged Trump to attack Iran over concerns about Iran's military capabilities. Trump had previously declared in June 2025 that limited strikes had "completely obliterated Iran's nuclear capability." By Sunday, the conflict had resulted in three U.S. service member deaths and hundreds of Iranian casualties, with Iran launching retaliatory attacks on Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

events.title: Trump administration claimed Iran posed "imminent threat" without supporting intelligence
events.summary: Trump framed the military campaign as necessary to eliminate "imminent threats" from Iran, destroy its missile capability, and prevent nuclear weapons, claiming Iran had been developing missiles that could "soon reach the American homeland." However, three sources familiar with intelligence reports told Reuters the claim is exaggerated. CNN reported separately that there is no intelligence to suggest Iran is pursuing an ICBM program to hit the U.S. at this time. An unclassified 2025 Defense Intelligence Agency assessment, which multiple sources confirmed has not been updated, said Iran could potentially develop a "militarily viable" ICBM by 2035, using existing space-launch vehicles, if it decided to pursue one. Even with assistance from China or North Korea, one source told Reuters, Iran would likely need at least eight years to produce something operationally viable at ICBM level. Secretary of State Marco Rubio declined to address the DIA assessment directly and did not give a timeline.
events.why_relevant: The administration's public justification for military action contradicts available U.S. intelligence assessments, undermining the factual basis for war and raising questions about truthfulness in national security decision-making.

events.title: Strait of Hormuz disrupted; shipping halted and oil prices surge
events.summary: The Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly 20% of global oil passes daily, became functionally disrupted as the IRGC broadcast warnings that passage was not allowed. More than 200 vessels including oil tankers and liquefied gas carriers anchored in and around the strait. Major tanker owners, oil and gas majors, and trading houses suspended shipments. Japan's three largest shipping companies—Nippon Yusen, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, and Kawasaki Kisen—halted operations through the strait. Container lines diverted away from highest-risk corridors. War-risk insurance costs for tankers jumped 25 to 50 percent. Brent crude surged roughly 8% on open with spikes around 10% reported in the immediate reaction window. events.title: DHS purchased warehouses and planned large-scale detention facility expansion
